doc.title: Houston Person Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Wrap-up banter, dancing and Basie learning from dancers
summary: Person jokes about a gig, says he never learned to dance but loves watching, and Rowe notes Basie learned tempos from dancers.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: Well is there’s anything else that you’d like to ask me before we wrap up here?
Yeah, give me a gig. Am I coming back in April? That’s what I want to know.
That’s what you want to know. Well I look forward to seeing you tomorrow night on the stage, and if I get up and start dancing I hope—
I’m going to play something slow and pretty for you, and you can dance. Are you going to dance for me now?
You know it’s funny I don’t dance much. Usually I’m on the playing end of things, but I do like to move to the music.
Well I don’t dance. I never learned. I’m a little shy too I guess.
Yeah I know I can tell.
Yeah, but getting out on the floor man. But I love to see people dance. That really gets to me.
Well the stories are, there are many stories on how fellows like Basie and everything learned from the dancers what tempos worked.
Yeah. You do. They’ll give it to you. Yeah I love it.
